conventions.convention: R(X,Y)Z = ∇X∇YZ − ∇Y∇XZ − ∇[X,Y]Z; Rm(X,Y,Z,W) = g(R(X,Y)Z,W). The Jacobi equation is D²J + R(J,T)T = 0, and the round sphere has positive sectional curvature.

The radial Jacobi tensor uses dimension n ≥ 2, a unit-speed geodesic, normal initial derivatives, A(0) = 0 and transported A′(0) = identity. The radial Riccati operator is A′A⁻¹ only at positive times before the first conjugate instant.
Δg = divg gradg = traceg Hess, with no minus sign. Distance Hessians and Laplacians are asserted off the base point and cut locus; positive-curvature comparisons additionally exclude the model pole.
The model density is sn_k(r)^(n−1). For k > 0 its positive domain ends at π/√k, and V*_k(r) = V_k(min(r,π/√k)); for k ≤ 0 there is no saturation.

Comparison triangles have positive sides and strict triangle inequalities. For k > 0 every side is < π/√k and the perimeter is < 2π/√k. Uniqueness allows orientation-reversing isometries. Lower sectional curvature gives actual angles ≥ model angles and fixed-angle opposite sides ≤ model opposite sides.
Riemannian volume is a Radon Borel measure; its completion has a separately specified domain. The polar integration supplier applies to Borel nonnegative functions and may discard the null cut locus.

Perfect means derived-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective left modules. Cochain shift has X[1]^n = X^(n+1) and negated differential; internal shift has (M{r})_d = M_(d−r). Graded maps and differentials have internal degree zero.
Triangle K0 imposes [Y] = [X] + [Z] for X → Y → Z → X[1]; split K0 imposes biproduct relations, while G0 imposes short-exact-sequence relations.

Hochschild bar degree j ≥ 0 contributes total cochain degree −j: n = i−j and D = dF + (−1)^i b. Internal grading contributes no super signs. The separate indices give a filtration, not generally a decomposition of hyperhomology.

Cyclicity assumes AC and finite projectivity on the indicated right sides only. Rotation occurs after coinvariants, with sign (−1)^pq for module double bars, (−1)^((i−p)(l−q)) for total complexes, and (−1)^il for termwise Hochschild homology.

load_bearing.statement: Assume ACω. For the radial Jacobi tensor along a unit-speed geodesic in dimension n ≥ 2, with 0 in its interval, S = A′A⁻¹ satisfies S′ + S² + Rγ = 0 before the first positive conjugate instant; S is self-adjoint and S(t) = t⁻¹ identity + O(t) as t ↓ 0.

Assume ACω. On a complete, connected, boundaryless Riemannian n-manifold, n ≥ 2, with Ric ≥ (n−1)k g, for every p the ratio vol(B(p,r))/V*_k(r), r > 0, is well defined and nonincreasing, tends to 1 at zero, and is constant on [π/√k,∞) when k > 0. In particular vol(B(p,r)) ≤ V*_k(r).

Assume ACω. On a complete, connected, boundaryless Riemannian n-manifold, n ≥ 2, at q off p and Cut(p), put t0 = d(p,q), with t0 < π/√k if k > 0. Radial sectional curvature ≥ k along the minimizing geodesic gives Hess r(X,X) ≤ ct_k(t0)g(X,X) for X normal to its terminal velocity; radial curvature ≤ k gives the reverse inequality. Hess r(grad r,·) = 0 off p and Cut(p).

Assume ACω. For unit-speed geodesics in two n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, n ≥ 2, and normal Jacobi fields with zero initial values and equal positive initial-derivative norms, if every radial sectional curvature of the first is ≥ every radial sectional curvature of the second and the first has no conjugate instant in (0,T], then |J1(t)| ≤ |J2(t)| on [0,T], and J2 has no zero in (0,T].

Assume ACω. In a complete, connected, boundaryless Riemannian manifold of dimension ≥ 2 with K ≥ k, let γ:[0,L] → M be unit-speed minimizing and o a third point. If its three side lengths admit the defined comparison triangle, then d(o,γ(t)) ≥ d_k(ō,γ̄(t)) for every t ∈ [0,L].

For every unital associative ring A, D_perf(A) is an essentially small strictly full triangulated subcategory of D(A-Mod), with the graded analogue. Every derived morphism between bounded finite-projective representatives is represented by a chain map uniquely up to homotopy, and its cone is again such a representative. No global-dimension hypothesis is required.

For any unital associative ring A, degree-zero inclusion induces K0_split(Proj_fg(A)) ≅ K0_tri(D_perf(A)); its inverse is the alternating class of the terms of a bounded finite-projective representative. The same holds for finite graded projectives and graded perfect complexes with degree-zero maps. Neither finite global dimension nor Noetherianity is required.

For every essentially small abelian category C, under the standing bounded-derived localization size convention, degree-zero inclusion induces G0(C) ≅ K0_tri(D^b(C)), with inverse [X] ↦ Σn (−1)^n[H^n(X)]. Enough projectives, enough injectives, Noetherianity and finite global dimension are unnecessary.

Assume AC. For a field k, unital associative k-algebras A,B, an (A,B)-bimodule M finite projective on the right over B, and a (B,A)-bimodule N finite projective on the right over A, the stated single- and double-bar constructions are projective resolutions on the corresponding enveloping-algebra sides. After coinvariants, cyclic rotation with sign (−1)^pq gives natural, involutive-up-to-homotopy comparisons and HH_j(A,M⊗B N) ≅ HH_j(B,N⊗A M) for every j ≥ 0. No left projectivity is required.

Assume AC. For a field k, a unital associative k-algebra A and a bounded complex F of k-central A-bimodules with internal-degree-zero differentials, the reindexed bar tensor total identifies with T(A,F) through the bar-to-Hochschild map multiplied by (−1)^ip. Any supplied bounded-above projective right-Ae resolution computes the same hyperhomology, canonically and naturally up to chain homotopy. Bounded coefficient quasi-isomorphisms induce hyperhomology isomorphisms, preserving internal grading when the map has internal degree zero.

concerns.concern: The normality derivation invokes thm-algebraic-symmetries-of-the-riemann-tensor, whose opened Statement assumes ACω, but this Definition states no such premise. The geometric page calls these interfaces choice-free. Either propagate the supplier qualification or give the needed choice-free local skewness derivation.

The Statement and conclusion say 'No completeness, compactness or choice hypothesis is used', while F3 and step 1.1 invoke the ACω-qualified algebraic-symmetry supplier. The local last-slot skewness argument can be supplied directly, but the current citation does not discharge its premise.

No ACω premise is stated, although F2 and F5 invoke the ACω-qualified sectional-curvature and algebraic-symmetry items. The local curvature identities may admit a choice-free derivation; that derivation or explicit premise propagation is currently missing.

The interval hypothesis permits I = [−1,0], but conclusion 2 defines the positive-time remainder on an interval (0,δ), outside the declared domain of S. A positive interval to the right of zero is needed for this formulation. Also the Statement's gloss 'Rγ(X)=R(X,γ′)' omits the final γ′ slot and is ill-typed.

Step 2.1 asserts that A = {t : u(s) ≥ v(s) > 0 for all 0 < s ≤ t} is nonempty 'by step 1.2', but step 1.2 establishes only positivity and u/v → 1. On that initial positive interval, the Wronskian identity gives h′ ≥ 0 and then (u/v)′ ≥ 0, which supplies the missing initial inequality.

Assertion 2 covers general nonscalar R2, but step 5.1's continuation uses the scalar function f from the special case R2 = k identity. General continuation is not written. On the common nonsingular interval, tracing S2 ≥ S1 gives det Y2 ≥ det Y1 > 0, ruling out an earlier singularity of Y2.

Step 1.1 writes the curvature term as sn_k times k(g(T,T)J_k−g(J_k,T)T), although J_k already equals sn_k Φw; this inserts an extra sn_k and does not yield the following displayed cancellation. In the second-form Statement, 'these conclusions extend to t=t_f' also needs to exclude the sectional-curvature statement when J(t_f)=0: its displayed two-plane then does not exist.

F5 says that if F is an immersion, 'F is then a local isometry from (N,F*g) to (M,g)'. The cited pullback proposition proves only that F*g is Riemannian. An immersion such as a Euclidean line into a Euclidean plane is not a local diffeomorphism and hence not a local isometry under the opened definition. Equal dimensions/local diffeomorphism must remain explicit.

The Statement omits nonemptiness, although the library permits empty connected manifolds and def-metric-bounded-diameter defines diameter only for nonempty bounded subsets. Step 1.1 also assumes a diameter value before boundedness has been proved; the cited definition supplies no infinite diameter. A point-pair argument avoids that circular domain use.

Step 7.1 says Cauchy–Schwarz equality holds 'exactly for linearly independent x,y, that is for y=±x'. The opened Cauchy–Schwarz supplier says linearly dependent. The written assertion is false, although the intended antipodal computation is clear.

The Statement classifies 'Its geodesics' as the displayed vertical curves and semicircles up to affine reparametrization, and F4 requires the reparametrization slope to be nonzero. Constant geodesics are consequently omitted. Step 4.1 checks only unit initial velocities and then concludes completeness for every maximal geodesic without stating the zero-velocity case.

Part 3 calls g = dr² + (sn_k(r)²/r²)σ an equivalent polar formula while defining σ as the metric of the unit tangent sphere. With that definition the angular factor is sn_k(r)²σ; at k=0 the written formula incorrectly gives dr²+σ instead of dr²+r²σ. Steps 1.2 and 1.3 also assert B0(R) ⊂ Dp, although the opened cut-domain definition excludes zero; the origin must be handled separately using d exp at zero.

Given defines R = π/√k and simultaneously names S_R^n as the model sphere of radius R. F11 then asserts 1/R² = k, which is false for that R. Step 1.2 locally redefines R = 1/√k, while later tangent-ball and gluing steps reuse R as the diameter, so the model construction is not consistently typed. F2 additionally writes V_k(R)=V_k(min{s,π/√k}) for 0<s≤R, which is false for s<R.

F4 strengthens the cut-point supplier to say that when conjugacy occurs at time t, 'the endpoint is a cut point'. The opened source concludes only c_q(v) ≤ t without a minimizing-at-t hypothesis. On the unit sphere, t=2π is conjugate to the start, but the endpoint is the start itself, not its antipodal cut point. The proof's relevant segments are minimizing; that qualification must be retained in the stated fact.

Step 1.3 says an orthonormal pair on a two-dimensional tangent space is 'the only orthonormal pair up to signs'. Rotations give other orthonormal pairs. The intended statement is that the tangent two-plane is unique, not its orthonormal basis.

F2 cites thm-nonnegative-continuous-with-zero-integral-vanishes for a function integrated over a manifold, but the opened theorem is only about a continuous function on a real interval. The needed manifold implication follows immediately from continuity and positive volume of nonempty open sets; that argument or the appropriate supplier is missing.

F9 says the inverse image of an open subset of R under the ball indicator is one of ∅, B(p,r), or M. An open interval containing 0 but not 1 has inverse image M\B(p,r), omitted from that list. The indicator is Borel, but the asserted enumeration is false.

F7 says the ball indicator's open-set inverse images are among ∅, B(p,r), and M. The complement M\B(p,r) is also possible, for an open interval containing 0 but not 1. The measurable-indicator justification needs that fourth case.

Step 1.1 asserts cos x ≤ 1 'with equality at the origin only', although cos(2π)=1. Step 1.6 writes cs_k(a±b)=cs_k(a)cs_k(b)±k sn_k(a)sn_k(b); the sign must be ∓, as its own F3 correctly states. These are false supporting identities despite the subsequent intended calculations.

The remark says 'This page proves no upper curvature comparison' and 'Its only conclusion with a sphere in it is Cheng's maximal-diameter rigidity'. The page also proves upper-sectional-curvature Hessian/conjugate comparisons and the separate sectional Toponogov diameter-rigidity corollary. The scope summary is inconsistent with the assigned content.

The explanatory sentence says the cochain and internal shifts 'produce different classes' without qualification. They act on different structures, but their classes need not differ, for example on the zero object. Keep the structural distinction without a universal claim of unequal classes.

The displayed resolution labels the final arrow A → S as multiplication by ε. Since εS=0, that map is zero and is not the augmentation A → A/(ε). The displayed complex is therefore not an exact resolution as written, although the verification uses the quotient augmentation.

F4 says the Hochschild boundary of the ground field is multiplication by the alternating sum, '0 for odd j and 1 for even j', without restricting j≥1. The degree-zero boundary is b0=0, as its own step 3.1 correctly uses. State the positive-degree restriction.
